Barrick mobilises mining contractor for the Lumwana expansion

By a staff reporter, 18 September 2026

Barrick Mining Corporation has started to mobilise a contract mining fleet for the expansion of the Lumwana copper mine in North-Western Province. The expansion will turn Lumwana into a super pit with a new process plant.

The contractor will bring 60 haul trucks, eight large excavators and a fleet of drills to the site before the end of 2026. Barrick said that the contractor will move waste rock from the pre-strip of the new pit while the company builds the process plant.

Barrick expects first production from the expansion in 2028. The company said that the expansion will double the copper output of the mine and extend its life by more than 30 years.

The mine manager said that the fleet will use about 20 million litres of diesel each year during the pre-strip. Barrick will appoint a fuel supplier for the expansion through a tender in the first half of 2027.

Local business associations in Solwezi and Kalumbila asked Barrick to reserve a part of the contracts for Zambian companies. Barrick said that it will publish its local content plan before the end of the year.
